evidence_quotes: A total of 39 significant earthquakes (magnitude 5.0 or greater) rattled the globe over the past 30 days
The strongest event — a magnitude 6.2 — struck near Nikolski, Alaska on January 25
the period's average magnitude held at a moderate 5.33
Tobelo, Indonesia led all hotspots with 6 recorded events, including a M5.7 on February 14
January 27 was the single busiest day, with 4 separate M5.0+ events spanning Indonesia, the Solomon Islands, Russia, and the Mariana Islands
La Tirana, Chile produced two M6.1 events (January 30 and February 2) within just three days
Tsunami alerts were triggered three times — near the Kermadec Islands (M5.7, Feb 8), New Britain/PNG (M5.5, Feb 3), and Tual, Indonesia (M5.5, Jan 27)
the M5.0 near Levídion, Greece (Feb 13, depth ~25 km) and the M5.2 off Honshu, Japan (Feb 12, depth ~3 km)
criticisms: The report states 'January 27 was the single busiest day, with 4 separate M5.0+ events spanning Indonesia, the Solomon Islands, Russia, and the Mariana Islands.' The digest daily_counts confirm 4 events on Jan 27, but the sample_events for that day show Tobelo Indonesia, Lata Solomon Islands, Kuril'sk Russia, and Tual Indonesia — NOT the Mariana Islands. The Mariana Islands events appear on Jan 28 and Jan 30. This is a minor but verifiable inaccuracy in the regional attribution for Jan 27.
The report says 'the M5.2 off Honshu, Japan (Feb 12, depth ~3 km)' — the digest shows depth 2.7 km, so rounding to ~3 km is acceptable but slightly imprecise.

The report characterizes the Kermadec Islands, New Britain/PNG, and Tual events as occurring in 'shallow-water settings.' While the depths are indeed shallow (5.7 km, 7.4 km, and 5.4 km respectively), the phrase 'shallow-water settings' conflates water depth with earthquake focal depth — a minor interpretive overreach not directly supported by the digest.
